 COMMON JUDGMENT
These petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act seeking compensation for the injuries caused in a road traffic accident.
Both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

2. The case of the petitioner is that on 14.07.2021 at about 00.10 a.m. (mid night), when the petitioner and deceased were proceeding in Hamaha R15 motorcycle bearing Regn. No.
KA-05-HY-4333 on Kanakapura mian road, Opp. Metro Pilar No.100, near Giriyas Show room,
Bengaluru at that time a Bharat Benz Lorry bearing Regn. No. KA-03- AF-8560 parked in the middle of the road without parking lights on or any indication, the rider of the motorcycle could not notice whether the lorry was moving or stopped, as it was dark night and inspite of the efforts made by him, his motorcycle rammed on the rear side of the lorry.
As a result, the petitioner and deceased suffered grievous head and bodily injuries and the rider of motorcycle in MVC No.1955/2022 died on the spot.
3. The petitioner in MVC No.1954/2022 was taken to NIMHANS hospital, Bangalore and the petitioner treated with conservative.
Due to accidental injuries, petitioner is suffering from disability and discomforts and lost his earnings.
The petitioner (in MVC No1954/2022 was working in a sales consultant and earning Rs.20,000/-p.m.

The petitioner (in MVC No.1955/2022 was working in a Sales Consultant and earning Rs.20,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, petitioners in both case are unable to do their normal work and lost the income.
Hence prays to award the compensation of Rs.20 lakhs in MVC No.1954/22 and Rs.80 lakhs in MVC No.1955/22 from the respondents.

sentences.text: 12. In this regard, on perusal of the documents, the accident has been taken place on 14.07.2021 at about 00.10 a.m (mid-night).
The brother of deceased Jagadeesh by name Anand K.L lodged complaint before the Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic PS as per Ex.P2.

According to the complaint Ex.P2, the deceased was riding the motorcycle along with the pillion rider PW.1 Harshith Gowda @ Harshith Kumar on Kanakapura Main road, from Talaghattapura towards Doddakallasandra in a speed manner, near Giriyas Show room metro pillar No.200 and hit to the back side of the lorry, due to which, the rider Jagadeesh sustained grievous head injury and succumbed at the spot and the pillion rider i.e., PW.1/Harshith Kumar sustained grievous injuries.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that the complaint has been lodged by the brother of deceased Jagadeesh against deceased himself and later on,
the petitioner colluding with the owner of the lorry and the police filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
13.

On the other hand, learned counsel for petitioner argued that the complainant Anand. brother of deceased Jagadeesh though has given complaint against deceased only, but he is not an eye witness and he has given the complaint on the say of the police and public and hence Ex.P2 complaint cannot be acceptable and believable.
Even thereafter, the police have conducted thorough and detailed investigation and submitted charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle lorry.

14. In this regard, on perusal of the evidence and materials on record, admittedly,
earlier the brother of the deceased Jagadeesh has lodged the complainant as per Ex.P2 against the deceased Jagadeesh only by contending that Jagadeesh was riding the motorcycle in a high speed and hit to the back of the Lorry.
But it is material to note here that Anand the complainant is not an eye witness to the accident.
Even the said Anand complainant has not stated from whom he received the information about the accident.
The said Anand simply stated that he enquired the public and traffic police.
But they are not eye witness to the incident.

Hence, merely based on the Ex.P2, this court cannot come to the conclusion that the accident has taken place due to the sole rash and negligence of the rider of the motorcycle deceased Jagadeesh only.
The investigating officer after thorough and detailed investigation has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is material to note here that the deceased who was riding the motor cycle was succumbed at the spot and the pillion rider who is only eye witness to the incident had sustained head injuries was taken to the hospital and soon after the accident, he was not in a condition to state anything with regard to the cause of the accident.

Admittedly, the accident has been taken place at 00.10 am midnight, except the pillion rider and the driver of the lorry no other persons might have present at the spot, as such there may be no eye witness except deceased, Pw.1 and driver of lorry.
Hence, the complaint lodged by the brother of the deceased Jagadeesh cannot be believable and acceptable.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent has not at all disputed Ex.P5 and seizure of the CCTV footage from the spot.

Even it is clearly stated in Ex.P5 that CCTV footage was put on in the Giriyas Showroom and it was seen from the camera on 14.07.2021 at about 1.00 a.m. cross near the Giriyas Showroom, the driver of the lorry has parked the lorry without giving any lights signals and at that time the rider of the motor cycle came and hit to the right back portion of the lorry and the lorry number and motorcycle number was not seen properly.
The eye witness Sri Somashekhara has identified the accident and the same video was transferred to the Pen-drive and Pen-drive was seized.

19. Apart from this, on perusal of the sketch Ex.P4 it clearly shows that the the lorry was parked on the left side middle of the road which clearly demonstrate that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent parking of the lorry in the left side middle of the road.
Moreover at the time of the accident it was dark night.
Even Ex.P4 is not at all denied and disputed by the respondent counsel and even respondent is not examined driver of lorry and to disprove the evidence of PW.1.
Further though respondent counsel has recalled the stage and summons has been issued to the witness investigating officer.

But, in spite of several opportunity given to the respondent, respondent failed to secure the witness before the court and examine him to prove that the charge sheet filed by the investigating officer is collusive and defective.
Even no materials and evidence were brought on record to disprove that the charge sheet is collusive and defective.
Even the respondent would have taken the copy of the pen-drive and would have produced to disprove the evidence of the PW.1.

The very manner and cause of the accident stated by the PW.1 clearly demonstrate that the accident has been taken place due to rash and negligent parking of the vehicle in the left side middle of the road.

Even it is not the case of the respondent that the driver of the lorry has not at all parked the vehicle or else have parked lorry on the road by keeping any barricades, reflectors and signals to safeguard the interest on the traffic moving on the road.
20. At one point of time, the respondent counsel has taken the contention that the lorry was moving slowly, but respondent has not proved the same by examining the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further at another point of time, respondent has taken the contention that the vehicle is not at all involved in the accident and the petitioner while try to overtake the ongoing vehicle hit to the right back side of the lorry.
The respondent by taking the above said contention himself admitted about the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

Even the owner of the vehicle has given the reply to 133 notice as per Ex.P7 admitting the involvement of the vehicle and also Prabhakaran N was driving the vehicle at the time of accident.
21.

The evidence and material on record, clearly shows that lorry was parked on the road without keeping any barricades, reflectors and signals to safeguard the interest on the traffic moving on the road and apart from this, it was dark night.

Precautions prescribed under Section 122 of MV Act read with the relevant Rules have to be followed by the driver and owner of the stationed vehicle,
particularly on a highway.

A duty is cast on the driver as well as the owner of such a vehicle to ensure that such a vehicle is towed away as immediately as practicable and not left abandoned or unattended, particularly on a highway where vehicles are permitted to move at a faster place than on other roads.

In the alternative, some other form of external lighting ought to have been provided so Harshith Gowda Alias Harshith Kumar V.S vs R.K Infra on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59783839/

Further in the judgment of the Gujarat High Court in Premlata Nilamchand Sharma vs. Hirabhai Ranchhodbhai Patel, [1983 ACJ 290] and the judgment of the Delhi High Court in Pushpa Rani Chopra vs. Anokha Singh, [1975 ACJ 396], Hon'ble Apex Court held that where the place was dark and the vehicle was parked without any sign or indication to warn other road users, negligence is on the driver of the parked vehicle and not the driver of any vehicle which dashes into such parked vehicle.

sentences.text: In view of the ratio held in the above decision in the present case, admittedly lorry was parked on the road without any sign or indication to warn other road users.
Moreover it was dark night.

Under such circumstances, certainly, it can be held that accident had been caused wholly due to the negligence on the driver of the lorry who had parked the lorry on the road without any indicator and barricade.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused wholly due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-03-AF-8560.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

25. Issue No.2 in MVC No. 1954/2022 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-03-AF-8560.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
26. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

So far as the age of petitioner by name Harshith Gowda @
Harshith Kumar V.S., is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 24 years.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.12, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 10.02.1999 and the accident took place on 14.07.2021.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 22 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was working in a Sales consultant and earning Rs.20,000/-p.m. and lost his earnings due to the injuries suffered in the accident.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

28. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e.,left front EDH with left frontal bone outer and inner table fracture with no mass effect/midline shift.
The said injuries are described as grievous in nature.
As per Ex-P11 discharge summary, petitioner Harishth Gowda., treated as conservatively.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony due to the injuries sustained by him on account of the accidental injuries.

The petitioner being 22 years,
certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
29. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and as per Ex.P11 Discharge summary, he took treatment at Deepasri Multispecialities hospitals as inpatient from 14.07.2021 to 15.07.2021 for a period of 2 days and it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.75,000/- (15,000 X 5) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
30. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner Harshith Gowda @ Harshith Kumar V.S.. is a resident of No.VTC Nittur, Virajpet, Kodagu, and has taken treatment at Deepasri Hospital,
Bengaluru on 14.07.2021 and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of treatment, the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.5,000/- under this head.
31. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS AND MARRIAGE PROSPECT:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Looking into the young age of the petitioner, the petitioner being unmarried and the injuries sustained by the petitioner to his face certainly would have cause disfiguration and which would certainly impact on his marriage prospect.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
32. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical bills Ex-P14 for Rs.23,374/- and Ex-P15-prescriptions.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.23,374/- under the head of medical expenses.

The evidence and material on record, clearly shows that lorry was parked on the road without keeping any barricades, reflectors and signals to safeguard the interest on the traffic moving on the road and apart from this, it was dark night.
Precautions prescribed under Section 122 of MV Act read with the relevant Rules have to be followed by the driver and owner of the stationed vehicle,
